meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.
Vegetable stew for dinner?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начаться'.

examples.trans: War begins again!

examples.text: Спасибо, теперь для нас начинается новая жизнь.
examples.trans: Thank you, now a new life begins for us.
Our work is only just beginning.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'клад'). Common masculine noun meaning 'warehouse, storage' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это старый заброшенный склад за городом.
examples.trans: It is an old abandoned warehouse outside town.

examples.text: Хорошо, тогда встретимся на этом складе.
examples.trans: Fine, then we will meet at this warehouse.

examples.text: Ищи на складе и быстрее крутись!
examples.trans: Search in the storage and hustle faster!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
Can you smoke here?
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'toilet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where's the toilet?
The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step back, to move away
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step back, to move away', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: Step back from the car!
He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'a little; nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'finger; toe' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: My finger!
My finger hurts.
Ow! My finger!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

отрезать.gloss: to cut off, to slice off

meanings.en: to cut off, to slice off
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'резать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cut off, to slice off', paired with 'отрезать'.

examples.trans: Will you cut my ear off?
Cut me a slice of bread.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'first-aid kit, medicine chest' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Bring the first-aid kit from the bathroom.

examples.text: В машине всегда должна быть аптечка.
examples.trans: There must always be a first-aid kit in the car.
Yulia, bring the first aid kit quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I need your help.
Thanks for the help!
I really need your help.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish; course' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry to, take to', paired with 'относить'.

examples.text: Я сам отнесу блюдо в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry the dish into the dining room myself.
Take the documents to the boss.

examples.text: Я сейчас сам отнесу в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry it to the hall myself right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'едьмой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('seventh').

examples.trans: This is seventh.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.
Look, the woman at the seventh table!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small table, café table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello, hey', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Right, quiet, everyone! Hello?

examples.text: Алло, Танечка! В свои годы это нормально.
examples.trans: Hello, Tanechka! At my age that's normal.
Hello, Ilyusha, hi. It's Anikeev.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!
I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call', paired with 'позвать'.

examples.trans: What's your name?
My name is Lyosha.
Mum is calling you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'сьмой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('eighth').

examples.trans: This car is from the 2008 production year.

examples.text: Эта машина две тысячи восьмого года.
examples.trans: This car is from the year 2008.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'along; by; about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'readiness; doneness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
Table eight is ready to go.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'banquet, feast' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A festive banquet.

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.
A lavish banquet was hosted in the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

торопиться.gloss: to be in a hurry, to hurry

meanings.en: to be in a hurry, to hurry
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be in a hurry, to hurry', paired with 'поторопиться'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Don't rush!
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!
